[ COMPANY · 9 MOTHERS ]

AI mission systems. Built in Austin.

9 Mothers builds counter-drone defense systems for the modern battlefield — the engagements that legacy C-sUAS was never designed for. Hardware tempo measured in months, not decades.

[ MISSION ]

Defense must move at the speed of the threat.

  1. 01

    The threat moved.

    FPV drones rewrote close-range warfare in two years. Cheap, fast, expendable, autonomous. Legacy C-sUAS — built for fixed-wing intruders at altitude — doesn't engage them.

  2. 02

    Procurement didn't.

    The acquisition cycle that produced the last generation of air defense takes a decade. The threat iterates in weeks. The gap is the problem.

  3. 03

    We close it.

    Point defense engineered at infantry-mobile scale, priced for attrition, and shipped on software tempo. Built so operators can field it now — not after the next budget cycle.

[ APPROACH ]

Hardware on software tempo.

How we build determines what we can field. These are the disciplines we hold non-negotiable.

Software discipline. Hardware reality.
We build hardware the way modern software teams build product — small batches, fast cycle time, real telemetry, instrumented in the field. No multi-year waterfall.
Engineered for attrition.
Cost-per-shot, manufacturability, and serviceability are first-class design constraints, not afterthoughts. A weapon you can't afford to fire isn't a weapon.
Operator-first.
Designed with the people who will carry it, set it up, and use it under stress. Mass, setup time, and human factors are non-negotiable specs.
Vertically scoped.
We own perception, tracking, and engagement end-to-end so the kill chain is one system — not three vendors and an integrator.
